newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Scientologists protest as Kohl visits Sydney.
newsitem.headline: Scientologists protest as Kohl visits Sydney.

text.p: A group of around 30 Scientologists, some dressed in fake Nazi uniforms, greeted German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday as he visited Sydney harbour and the city's famous Opera House.
The group, protesting against Germany's refusal to recognise the U.S.-based Church of Scientology as a church, held up banners accusing Germany of abusing their human rights.
But Kohl ignored the protest, waving to well-wishers as he toured the landmark Opera House.

On the last full day of a five-day visit to Australia, Kohl flew into Sydney from the capital Canberra and enjoyed a harbour cruise with New South Wales state premier Bob Carr and former prime minister Paul Keating.
Kohl, accompanied by a delegation of around 50 business leaders, is on his 12th visit to the Asia-Pacific region since becoming Chancellor in 1982.
"Germany is the world's number two exporter, but the others are getting stronger and stronger and we need to visit future markets," Kohl told reporters.
"I am not German business's chief salesman but I can help break the ground."
Kohl leaves Sydney on Wednesday morning for New Zealand and will also visit Hong Kong before returning to Germany.
